title: Town landing page — choose the page structure
question: Same site identity on every card (pink #E58DB4, Inter, the existing header/footer/CTA box). The roll dealt three page structures for /elainlaakari-kristiinankaupunki/ + /sv/veterinar-narpes-kristinestad/. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: One-trip plan
options.lineage: the appointment-prep sheet a clinic hands a travelling client
options.thesis: The page IS the visit plan: five numbered steps from booking to driving home, with the reasons to come inside step 4.
options.viewport: H1 + one-line promise left, Call/Book buttons right; directly under them the step rail begins: 1 Book and tell us your town · 2 Bring your records · 3 Drive ~1 h (town chips with times) · 4 Exam, imaging and lab the same day (the 7-row service ledger with prices lives here) · 5 Home the same evening, findings sent to your vet. Emergency note as a flagged aside, FAQ and CTA box close the page.
options.risk: A plan can read as a process page and bury the why; the step-4 ledger must be visibly rich or the page feels administrative.

regions.label: step 5: home, findings to your vet · emergency aside

options.label: Pick your town
options.lineage: a regional service page with a municipality switch
options.thesis: One control at the top: tap your town, and the drive time, kilometres and on-call number rewrite everywhere on the page.
options.viewport: H1, then a row of town chips (Kristiinankaupunki · Kaskinen · Närpiö · Teuva · Karijoki · Isojoki) with the chosen town's drive time and km beside the Call/Book buttons. Below: the service grid, one-trip tips, working-with-your-vet, a town-specific emergency block, FAQ, CTA. Works without JS (all towns listed by default); each town deep-links (#teuva).
options.risk: One interactive control on a page that otherwise has none; if the chips look like links the reader bounces off the page instead of into it.

options.label: Sister page
options.thesis: Exactly the article-card composition the Vaasa and cat pages use: one column of prose with H2 sections, a price box, FAQ and the CTA box.
options.viewport: Centred article card: H1, two intro paragraphs, Call/Book buttons, then the H2 sections in order (worth the drive as a linked bullet list, one trip, your vet, emergencies, prices, FAQ), CTA box, back link. Nothing new to learn or maintain.
options.risk: On a phone it is a 700-word column; the first viewport proves nothing beyond the headline, and the town facts sit a long scroll down.

options.label: Boarding pass + gate board
options.thesis: A segmented pass and a live gate board.
options.viewport: A pass with a scannable block beside a reranking board.
options.risk: Owners do not identify with airports.
options.case: Loses both axes: no counterpart to a reranking board on a static clinic page, and the airport frame says nothing about pets.
options.kept: Labeled segments with tabular figures: drive times and prices set in tabular digits, each block labeled.

options.label: Creator hardware bench
options.thesis: Keycaps in a gunmetal chassis with one orange action key.
options.viewport: A strict keycap grid with one orange key.
options.risk: Fights the site's soft card language.
options.case: Loses both axes: a desk instrument's grid contradicts the committed identity and the mobile reader.
options.kept: One safety-orange action key: exactly one primary action per viewport (Book), everything else secondary.

options.label: HyperCard stack
options.thesis: Black-and-white cards linked by painted buttons.
options.viewport: A fixed card with hand-drawn borders.
options.risk: Adds clicks to a one-scroll page.
options.case: Loses both axes: one-bit black and white breaks the pink/Inter identity, and card-by-card navigation hides a page that must read in one scroll.
options.kept: Every card addressable: each town and section gets a deep link (#teuva, #hinnat).

options.label: Collider event display
options.viewport: A frozen collision in concentric rings.
options.risk: No honest mapping to a vet visit.
options.case: Loses both axes: a dark WebGL vacuum has no honest mapping to a clinic visit and costs rural 4G users the page.
options.kept: Pin labels to the thing they describe: each drive time sits on its town, not in a separate table.

options.label: Cephalopod skin display
options.thesis: A living skin that changes pattern with context.
options.viewport: A pale mantle blooming into patterns.
options.risk: Spectacle the task does not need.
options.case: Loses both axes: shaders are spectacle the task does not need and rural connections cannot afford.
options.kept: Context-dependent signal: the emergency block changes with the chosen town.

options.label: Sleeping city fold
options.thesis: Streets crease into blankets; districts dream their own weather.
options.viewport: A folded night map with stitched district names.
options.case: Loses both axes: a surreal night city contradicts the clinic's plain, honest voice and the daytime task.
options.kept: Each district carries its own facts: each town carries its own time, km and on-call number.
